title: falava, comia
intro: Portuguese has a second past tense, the imperfeito, for what used to happen or what was going on: *Quando era pequeno*, *morava no Porto* = When I was little, I lived in Porto.

tables.meaning: to eat (-ir verbs work the same: partia)
tables.caption: Imperfeito of comer

examples.en: I used to live in Porto.
I used to drink a lot of coffee.

examples.pt: Jogávamos à bola todos os dias.
A minha avó vivia perto da praia.
examples.en: My grandmother lived near the beach.

notes: *Eu* and *ele* have the same form (*eu falava*, *ele falava*), so say the person when it isn't clear.
Estar and *ir* are regular here: *estava*, *ia*. *Ler* too: lia, *lias*…
Time words that go with it: *antigamente* (in the old days), *quando era pequeno* (when I was little), *todos os dias*, *sempre*.

drills.en: When I was little, I lived in Porto.
I used to drink a lot of coffee.
We played football every day.
My grandmother lived near the beach.
Did you read a lot when you were little?
Before, I worked in an office.
Ana didn't use to eat meat.
They used to live in Lisbon.

title: era, tinha, estava, ia
summary: ser, ter, estar and ir in the imperfeito
intro: Only four verbs are irregular in the imperfeito: ser, *ter*, *vir* and *pôr*. Estar and *ir* are regular, but you'll use them all the time, so they're here too.

examples.pt: Quando era pequeno, tinha um cão.
examples.en: When I was little, I had a dog.

examples.pt: Íamos à praia todos os verões.
examples.en: We went to the beach every summer.

notes: The other two: *vir* → *vinha*, vinhas, *vinha*…; *pôr* → punha, punhas, punha…
Descriptions in the past use the imperfeito: O hotel *era bonito e tinha* piscina = The hotel was nice and had a pool.
Time and age in the past too: *Eram três horas*. *Tinha dez anos*.

drills.en: When I was little, I had a dog.
When I was little, I had a dog.
It was very hot yesterday.
We went to the beach every summer.
It was ten o'clock.

drills.after: vinte anos quando foi para Lisboa.
drills.en: She was twenty when she went to Lisbon.
Yesterday I was tired.
Before, I was a student.

title: fiz or fazia?
intro: Use the perfeito (*fiz*, *falei*) for a finished event: something that happened once, or at a clear moment. *Ontem fui ao cinema*.
Use the imperfeito (*fazia*, *falava*) for what used to happen, what was going on, and descriptions. *Ia ao cinema todos os sábados*. *Estava a chover*.
In a story, the imperfeito sets the scene and the perfeito says what happened: *Estava a ler quando o telefone tocou*.

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

examples.pt: Ia ao cinema todos os sábados.
examples.en: I used to go to the cinema every Saturday.
It was raining when I went out.

examples.pt: A casa era antiga e tinha um jardim.
examples.en: The house was old and had a garden.

notes: Quick test: if English could say "used to" or "was …ing", it's usually the imperfeito.
Words that point to the perfeito: *ontem*, *uma vez* (once), *de repente* (suddenly), em 2020. Words that point to the imperfeito: *sempre*, *todos os dias*, *antigamente*, *quando era pequeno*.

drills.en: Yesterday I went to the cinema.
drills.why: One finished event at a clear time (*ontem*): perfeito.

drills.en: When I was little, I went to the cinema every Saturday.
drills.why: Something that used to happen: imperfeito.

drills.en: It was raining when I went out.
drills.why: Setting the scene, what was going on: imperfeito.

drills.before: Estava a ler quando o telefone
drills.en: I was reading when the phone rang.
drills.why: What happened in the middle of the scene: perfeito.

drills.en: The house was old and had a garden.
In 2020 I came to Portugal for the first time.
drills.why: One event at a clear time: perfeito.

drills.en: I used to drink a lot of coffee.
Suddenly the power went off.

drills.before: Quando eu era criança, o meu avô
drills.en: When I was a child, my grandfather lived on a farm.
drills.why: What was the case at that time: imperfeito.

drills.en: Yesterday I stayed at home all day.
drills.why: A finished stretch of time (all day yesterday): perfeito.

drills.en: It was eleven o'clock and I was hungry.
drills.why: A state at that moment: imperfeito.

drills.en: It was her birthday yesterday.

title: estava a fazer, queria, podia
summary: was doing, and the polite imperfeito
intro: *Estava* a + verb = was doing, something going on at that moment: *Estava a dormir quando ligaste*.
Portugal also uses the imperfeito to be polite: *Queria um* café (I'd like a coffee), *Podia ajudar-me*? (Could you help me?), *Gostava de ir* (I'd like to go).
In everyday speech it often means "would": *Se tivesse tempo*, *ia contigo* = If I had time, I'd go with you. (*Tivesse* comes in a later topic.)

examples.en: I was asleep when you called.
I'd like to go to Sintra.

notes: *Gostava* de… is the usual way to say "I'd like to…" in Portugal: *Gostava* de visitar *os Açores*.
Brazil uses *gostaria* and poderia more. In Portugal those exist too but sound more formal.

drills.en: I was asleep when you called.
What were you doing?
We were making dinner when they arrived.
They were watching TV.
I'd like a coffee, please.
Could you help me?
I'd like to go to Sintra.
Would you like to live in Lisbon?
I'd like a coffee, please.

drills.after: a ler quando a luz foi abaixo.
drills.en: Last night I was reading when the power went off.
drills.why: What was going on when something happened: *estava* a.

drills.en: Could you help me, please?
If I had money, I'd buy a house by the beach.
drills.why: In everyday Portuguese the imperfeito often means "would".
